llm.summary: The skill is a coherent project-planning helper, but it automatically forwards brainstorming content into other skills and subagents without a clear confirmation gate.

dimensions.detail: The brainstorming, comparison, brief-writing, and quality-review functions fit the stated project-ideation purpose, but the workflow expands into War Room deliberation and project specification rather than stopping at a brief.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The artifact prominently documents automatic handoff to attune:war-room with all brainstorming context, automatic continuation to attune:project-specification, and a haiku-model review loop; these are disclosed in the body, but the triggers and short description understate the amount of delegation and continuation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown skill instructions and module prompts only; no executable scripts, dependencies, install hooks, or obfuscated code were present, and static/VirusTotal telemetry was clean.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: For a brainstorming skill, broad triggers such as planning and requirements can activate a workflow that shares potentially sensitive ideas, constraints, and approaches with additional LLM components and downstream skills.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs saving docs/project-brief.md and .attune/brainstorm-session.json; this local persistence is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but users should treat the saved session as potentially sensitive project data.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an opinionated Attune workflow that can move from brainstorming into War Room review and specification automatically. Use --standalone or explicitly tell the agent to stop after brainstorming if you do not want downstream handoffs, and use --skip-review if you do not want the review subagent. Avoid using it for confidential plans unless you are comfortable with the local .attune/brainstorm-session.json file and the documented sharing of brainstorming context with other LLM-driven components.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: War Room pressure testing is aligned with generating a validated brief, but the artifact requires automatic invocation and passing all brainstorming context, so the control concern is supported.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Automatic continuation into project specification goes beyond a bounded brainstorming session and explicitly avoids a confirmation prompt, although --standalone or an explicit stop request can bypass it.
[SDI-2] expected: The spec-review loop is a quality gate for planning documents, but it dispatches a subagent with spec content and allows iterative agent-side fixes before proceeding.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad triggers are real and increase surprise risk because this skill performs automatic handoffs and persistence, not just ideation.
[SQP-2] expected: Context sharing and local session saving are disclosed in the artifact, so they are not hidden, but they remain important privacy and control considerations for sensitive brainstorming.
